subtopics.title: What a GIS Is and the Two Kinds of Data

questions.question: The five verbs that define a GIS are:
A road drawn on a map versus the route number printed on it illustrates:
options: Spatial data (the drawing) versus attribute data (the label)

questions.question: A natural line feature and a constructed line feature would be, respectively:
options: A borehole and an urban block

questions.question: Raster data differs from vector data in that raster:
options: Builds the scene from a grid of equal cells, like the pixels of a photograph

questions.question: Data layering means:
options: Storing different themes of information in separate, stackable, georeferenced layers
Printing a map on several sheets of paper

questions.question: A layer containing every river, pan and reservoir should be named the:
Layers align perfectly when stacked because:
options: They are printed at different scales
They are drawn by the same cartographer
All layers are georeferenced to the same coordinate system
Each layer contains the same features

questions.question: When combining given layer sketches into one frame, the governing rule is:
options: Enlarge every feature slightly for clarity
Draw the layers side by side
Every feature keeps its own position, overlapping where the originals overlap

questions.question: A buffer around a line feature such as a stream or power line takes the shape of:
options: A corridor of chosen width along the feature
A circle centred on the feature

questions.question: A strip of deliberately empty land between houses and a floodplain is best explained as:
options: A buffer keeping development out of flood danger
Land too expensive to build on

questions.question: The request 'show every open erf larger than 400 square metres within 2 km of a taxi route' is an example of:
options: A query — fetching every feature that satisfies stated conditions

questions.question: Data integration must happen before querying because:
options: Queries only work on paper maps
Data from different sources must first sit in one system on one coordinate grid so the layers can talk

subtopics.title: Resolution, Data Manipulation and Answering GIS Questions

questions.question: Of two images of the same scene, the one with fewer pixels will be:
options: Blurrier, because each pixel is larger and the resolution lower
Sharper, because it stores less clutter

questions.question: To make an unclear area of an orthophoto more readable, the standard scale manipulation is to:
options: Reduce the scale to show more ground
Enlarge the scale — zoom in — so the same ground occupies more image
Convert the image to vector format

questions.question: Besides scale changes, data manipulation also includes:
options: Painting layers different colours by hand
Converting between data formats and reprojecting data onto another coordinate system
Printing the map at higher quality

questions.question: The three recurring GIS question types are:
options: Calculation, translation, and drawing to scale
Vocabulary definitions, application to the mapped area, and the practical layer redraw

subtopics.title: The Burger That Explains the Whole System

questions.question: The burger explains layering because:
options: Its layers are made separately but consumed together, aligned in one stack

questions.question: In the friend sentence, 'where she is standing' versus 'her name and number' separates:
'Drawings stay sharp when you zoom; photos eventually turn to blocks' contrasts:

subtopics.title: The Chalk Circle Around the Beehive

questions.question: The chalk circle around the beehive is a buffer because it:
options: Gives the danger a measured edge so the inside can be treated differently from the outside

questions.question: A cleared corridor beneath a high-voltage power line is:
options: A line-feature buffer keeping buildings out of the servitude

questions.question: Typing a song title into a music app parallels a GIS query because:
options: Both ask a database to fetch every item matching stated conditions
Both work without any stored data

questions.question: The 'unglamorous step' that must precede searching is:
options: Integration — loading all sources into one system on one grid

subtopics.title: Pixels, Zooming In and Free Marks

questions.question: The photographed bird dissolving into fuzzy squares when zoomed demonstrates:
options: Low resolution — too few pixels, each one large

questions.question: The professional reason sentence for the blurrier of two photographs is:
options: It is less clear because its pixels are larger and its resolution lower
It is less clear because it was taken at night
It is less clear because it is a vector image
It is less clear because the printer failed

questions.question: The six-idea story of the lesson runs:
options: Contours, bearings, gradients, scales, symbols, grids
Layers, spatial-plus-attribute data, vector and raster, buffers, queries, integration
Push, pull, site, situation, pattern, function
Capture, flood, erode, deposit, meander, rejuvenate

questions.question: The clinic in the running example is finally placed by:
options: The loudest voice at the council meeting
Stacked layers, exclusion buffers and a query returning flat, dry, reachable, unclaimed land
Guesswork refined by trial and error
